external_entities.name: colleagues
external_entities.description: People who sign in through the identity broker and use applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
external_entities.notes: The description does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

external_entities.name: franchise colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues from franchise stores who authenticate through their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system that supplies colleague and group membership changes overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

external_entities.name: franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: The identity provider operated by the franchise that vouches for franchise colleagues.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The description does not state which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, maintains group membership, signs tokens, and writes sign-ins to the audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The broker does not call back to check whether a colleague is still allowed. Leavers are removed through the overnight HR synchronisation, and tokens remain valid for twelve hours with no early revocation. The description does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: applications
processes.description: Applications consume broker-issued tokens and decide what colleagues may do from the groups in each token.
processes.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that allows holders of a store-manager token to change prices and void transactions across every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store containing the signing key used by the identity broker to sign tokens.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory containing colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Group membership is supplied from the HR system overnight rather than maintained there by hand.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route. Nobody has written down whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: Colleagues sign in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a signed-in colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token carries the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in.
data_flows.data_description: A token carrying the colleague's staff id and group list

data_flows.name: pass token
data_flows.description: Applications take the token issued by the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token
data_flows.notes: The description does not specify how the token is delivered to applications.
data_flows.data_description: A token carrying a staff id and group list

data_flows.name: administer stores
data_flows.description: A colleague uses the store admin console to change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.notes: A store-manager token works against every store because the console does not check which store the colleague belongs to.
data_flows.data_description: Store-manager authorization, price changes, and transaction voids

data_flows.name: read signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker uses the signing key kept in the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: fetch public half
data_flows.description: Applications fetch the public half of the signing key from the identity broker to check token signatures.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: Public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: send membership changes
data_flows.description: The HR system supplies colleague and group membership changes to the identity broker overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.
data_flows.notes: The broker pulls the changes once a night.

data_flows.name: update directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker stores colleagues and their group memberships in its directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The description does not state what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

data_flows.name: vouch for colleague
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for franchise colleagues.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them

data_flows.name: federated sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider supplies a sign-in assertion accepted by the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in
data_flows.notes: The description does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: own devices at home
trust_boundaries.description: The home-device environment from which colleagues may sign in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise stores
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise environment whose colleagues and identity provider are admitted to the system.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

assumptions.assumption: The directory contains confidential data because it stores colleagues and their group memberships, which identify or describe people.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory keeps colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The key store contains confidential data because it stores the token-signing key, which is a secret.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker keeps a signing key in the key store.
